e102.desc: TARTRAZINE is a synthetic lemon yellow azo dye primarily used as a food coloring.

e120.desc: CARMINE, also called cochineal, cochineal extract, crimson lake or carmine lake, natural red 4, C.I. 75470, or E120, is a pigment of a bright-red color obtained from the aluminium salt of carminic acid

e127.desc: ERYTHROSINE, is an organoiodine compound, specifically a derivative of fluorone. It is cherry or melon-pink synthetic, primarily used for food coloring.

e131.desc: PATENT BLUE V is a dark bluish synthetic triphenylmethane dye used as a food coloring. It is not widely used, but in Europe it can be found in Scotch eggs, certain jelly sweets, blue Curaçao, certain jello varieties -though not in actual Jell-O brand products-, among others.

e133.desc: BRILLIANT BLUE FCF -Blue 1- is an organic compound classified as a blue triarylmethane dye, reflecting its chemical structure. Known under various commercial names, it is a colorant for foods and other substances.

e140i.desc: CHLOROPHYLL is any of several related green pigments found in cyanobacteria and the chloroplasts of algae and plants. Chefs use chlorophyll to color a variety of foods and beverages green, such as pasta and spirits.

n.en: Copper complexes of chlorophylls and chlorophyllins

e142.desc: GREEN S is a green synthetic coal tar triarylmethane dye with the molecular formula C27H25N2O7S2Na. It can be used in mint sauce, desserts, gravy granules, sweets, ice creams, and tinned peas.

e150.desc: CARAMEL is a medium to dark-orange confectionery product made by heating a variety of sugars.

e150a.desc: Caramel color or caramel coloring is a water-soluble food coloring.

e161b.desc: LUTEIN is a xanthophyll and one of 600 known naturally occurring carotenoids. Lutein is extracted from the petals of African marigold -Tagetes erecta-. It is approved for use in the EU and Australia and New Zealand. In the United States lutein may not be used as a food coloring for foods intended for human consumption, but can be added to animal feed.

e170i.desc: CALCIUM CARBONATE is a chemical compound with the formula CaCO3.

e200.desc: SORBIC ACID, or 2‚4-hexadienoic acid, is a natural organic compound used as a food preservative. It has the chemical formula CH3-CH-4CO2H.

e202.desc: POTASSIUM SORBATE is the potassium salt of sorbic acid, chemical formula CH3CH=CH−CH=CH−CO2K.

e203.desc: CALCIUM SORBATE  is the calcium salt of sorbic acid. Calcium sorbate is a polyunsaturated fatty acid salt.

e211.desc: SODIUM BENZOATE is a substance which has the chemical formula NaC7H5O2

e220.desc: Sulphur dioxide is a gas derived from burning elemental sulphur or as a byproduct of metal smelting and fossil fuel combustion. Industrially, it's produced by burning sulphur in oxygen or via the contact process used for sulphuric acid manufacturing. It has a sharp, pungent smell and, in concentrated form, a slightly acidic, irritating taste. In food, it acts as a preservative, antioxidant, and antimicrobial agent, commonly used in dried fruits, wine, fruit juices, and processed potatoes to prevent browning and spoilage. Nutritionally, it contributes no calories, vitamins, or minerals; it's regulated globally as a food additive with permitted maximum levels.

e221.desc: SODIUM SULFITE is a soluble sodium salt of sulfurous acid -sulfite- with the chemical formula Na2SO3.

e222.desc: SODIUM BISULFITE is a chemical compound with the chemical formula NaHSO3.

e223.desc: Sodium disulfite -E 223- is a synthetic white crystalline powder with no natural food source. It is produced by passing sulfur dioxide through sodium hydroxide or carbonate solution, then crystallizing the resulting sodium bisulfite. Its taste is sharply pungent, sulfurous and faintly salty. Worldwide, it serves as a preservative, antioxidant and anti-browning agent in wine, dried fruit, juices, potato products and shellfish, and occasionally as a dough conditioner. Codex, the EU and the US regulate its permitted levels and require sulfite labeling. It is used in trace amounts and provides no calories or nutritional value.

e224.desc: POTASSIUM METABISULFITE, K2S2O5, also known as potassium pyrosulfite, is a white crystalline powder with a pungent sulfur odour. The main use for the chemical is as an antioxidant or chemical sterilant.

e235.desc: NATAMYCIN is used in the food industry as a preservative.

e241.desc: GUM GUAICUM, or guaiac resin, is a substance produced from the tree species Guaiacum officinale.

e242.desc: DIMETHYL DICARBONATE is an organic compound which is a colorless liquid with a pungent odor at high concentration at room temperature. It is primarily used as a beverage preservative, processing aid, or sterilant

e250.desc: A synthetic salt manufactured industrially by reacting sodium hydroxide or sodium carbonate with nitrogen oxide gases, produced worldwide for food and industrial applications. It's typically supplied as a fine white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder. Sodium nitrite itself is essentially tasteless in the small quantities used, though it contributes to the characteristic tangy, savory flavor of cured meats through chemical reactions during processing. Widely used globally as a curing agent and preservative in bacon, ham, sausages, and other processed meats, where it inhibits bacterial growth -notably Clostridium botulinum- and stabilizes color. Nutritionally, it provides no caloric or nutrient value, serving solely a functional preservation role.

e251.desc: SODIUM NITRATE is the chemical compound with the formula NaNO3. Sodium nitrate is a food additive used as a preservative and colour fixative in cured meats and poultry

e252.desc: POTASSIUM NITRATE is a chemical compound with the chemical formula KNO3. The widespread adoption of nitrate use is more recent and is linked to the development of large-scale meat processing. potassium nitrate is still used in some food applications, such as salami, dry-cured ham, charcuterie.

e260.desc: ACETIC ACID, systematically named ethanoic acid, is a colourless liquid organic compound with the chemical formula CH3COOH -also written as CH3CO2H or C2H4O2-.

e262i.desc: SODIUM ACETATE, also abbreviated NaOAc,[8] is the sodium salt of acetic acid.

e263.desc: CALCIUM ACETATE is a chemical compound which is a calcium salt of acetic acid. Calcium acetate is used as a food additive, as a stabilizer, buffer and sequestrant, mainly in candy products.

e270.desc: An organic acid naturally occurring in fermented foods, first identified in sour milk, now produced globally through microbial fermentation. It's manufactured by fermenting carbohydrate sources like corn, sugarcane, or beets with lactic acid bacteria, followed by purification. Lactic acid has a sharp, tangy, sour taste and is used worldwide as an acidulant, preservative, and pH regulator in dairy products, baked goods, beverages, pickled vegetables, and processed meats. It also aids fermentation in foods like yogurt and sauerkraut. Nutritionally, it provides a negligible caloric contribution and no significant vitamins or minerals, functioning primarily as a flavoring and preservation agent rather than a nutrient source.

e281.desc: Sodium propanoate or SODIUM PROPIONATE is the sodium salt of propionic acid.

e282.desc: CALCIUM PROPIONATE has the formula Ca-C2H5COO-2. Calcium propionate is used as a preservative in a wide variety of products, including but not limited to:bread, other baked goods, processed meat, whey, and other dairy products.

e290.desc: CARBON DIOXIDE chemical formula CO2- is a colorless gas with a density about 60% higher than that of dry air.

e296.desc: MALIC ACID is an organic compound with the molecular formula C4H6O5. Malic acid has two stereoisomeric forms -L- and D-enantiomers-, though only the L-isomer exists naturally.

e300.desc: Ascorbic acid is a naturally occurring organic compound found in citrus fruits, berries, and vegetables such as peppers and broccoli. Commercially, it is produced industrially through fermentation of glucose -often derived from corn-, followed by chemical conversion steps, yielding a highly pure, food-grade powder. It has a mildly tart, sour taste, similar to citrus. Ascorbic acid is widely used as a food additive -E300- for its antioxidant properties, preventing browning and preserving freshness in juices, canned goods, and processed foods. Nutritionally, it is an essential water-soluble vitamin, contributing to collagen synthesis, immune function, and iron absorption across diverse global diets.

e301.desc: SODIUM ASCORBATE is one of a number of mineral salts of ascorbic acid -vitamin C-.

n.en: Fatty acid esters of ascorbic acid

e304i.desc: ASCORBYL PALMITATE is an ester formed from ascorbic acid and palmitic acid creating a fat-soluble form of vitamin C.

e316.desc: SODIUM ERYTHORBATE is the sodium salt of erythorbic acid. Sodium erythorbate is produced from sugars derived from different sources, such as beets, sugar cane, and corn. It is used predominantly in meats, poultry, and soft drinks.

e322.desc: is a generic term to designate any group of yellow-brownish fatty substances occurring in animal and plant tissues, and are used for smoothing food textures, dissolving powders -emulsifying-, homogeLECITHINnizing liquid mixtures, and repelling sticking materials. The term lecithin refers to a group of compounds found in every living organism, as they are part of the cell wall of all cells. Lecithin is commercially isolated -mainly- from soybeans or egg yolk.

e325.desc: SODIUM LACTATE is the sodium salt of lactic acid, and has a mild saline taste. It is produced by fermentation of a sugar source, such as corn or beets. It acts as a preservative, acidity regulator, and bulking agent.

e326.desc: POTASSIUM LACTATE is a compound with formula KC3H5O3. It is produced by neutralizing lactic acid which is fermented from a sugar source. Potassium lactate is commonly used in meat and poultry products to extend shelf life and increase food safety as it has a broad antimicrobial action. lactic acid and lactates can be consumed by all religious groups, vegans and vegetarians. Although the name refers to milk, it is not made from milk and thus suitable for people with milk allergy or lactose intolerance.

e331i.desc: MONOSODIUM CITRATE, more correctly, sodium dihydrogen citrate, is an acid salt of citric acid.

e331ii.desc: DISODIUM CITRATE, more properly, disodium hydrogen citrate, is an acid salt of citric acid with the chemical formula Na2C6H6O7. It is used as an antioxidant in food and to improve the effects of other antioxidants. It is also used as an acidity regulator and sequestrant. Typical products include gelatin, jam, sweets, ice cream, carbonated beverages, milk powder, wine, and processed cheeses.

e332ii.desc: POTASSIUM CITRATE -also known as tripotassium citrate- is a potassium salt of citric acid with the molecular formula K3C6H5O7. As a food additive, potassium citrate is used to regulate acidity. It is also used in many soft drinks as a buffering agent.

e334.desc: TARTARIC ACID is a white, crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many fruits, most notably in grapes, but also in bananas, tamarinds, and citrus

e336i.desc: POTASSIUM BITARTRATE, also known as potassium hydrogen tartrate, with formula KC4H5O6, is a byproduct of winemaking.

e339.desc: SODIUM PHOSPHATES is a generic term for a variety of salts of sodium -Na+- and phosphate -PO43−-.

e339i.desc: MONOSODIUM PHOSPHATE, also known as monobasic sodium phosphate and sodium dihydrogen phosphate, is an inorganic compound of sodium with a dihydrogen phosphate -H2PO4−- anion.

e339ii.desc: DISODIUM PHOSPHATE, or sodium hydrogen phosphate, or sodium phosphate dibasic, is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2HPO4.

e339iii.desc: TRISODIUM PHOSPHATE is the inorganic compound with the chemical formula Na3PO4.

e383.desc: CALCIUM GLYCERYLPHOSPHATE -or calcium glycerophosphate- is a mineral supplement for Calcium.

e392.desc: Derived from Rosmarinus officinalis, a Mediterranean evergreen shrub cultivated widely across Europe, North Africa, and increasingly in Asia and the Americas. The extract is produced by drying rosemary leaves and processing them through solvent or CO₂ extraction to isolate concentrated compounds, primarily carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid. It carries a robust, herbaceous flavor with piney, slightly peppery, and mildly bitter notes. Commonly used as a natural antioxidant and preservative in processed meats, oils, snacks, and sauces, it helps extend shelf life by slowing oxidation. Nutritionally, rosemary extract contains trace polyphenols and antioxidant compounds, though it's typically used in amounts too small to contribute meaningfully to daily nutrient intake.

e410.desc: Locust bean gum -E410-, also called carob gum, is a plant-derived hydrocolloid obtained from the endosperm of carob tree -Ceratonia siliqua- seeds, cultivated mainly around the Mediterranean, notably in Spain, Portugal, Italy, Morocco, and Turkey. Production involves removing the seed husk, separating the endosperm, milling it into a fine powder, and sometimes purifying it with alcohol. It is odorless and neutral in taste. Used worldwide as a thickener, stabilizer, and gelling agent, it appears in ice cream, cheeses, sauces, bakery fillings, and pet food. Nutritionally, it is almost entirely galactomannan soluble fiber, with negligible calories, protein, or fat at typical use levels.

e414.desc: GUM ARABIC, also known as acacia gum, arabic gum, gum acacia, acacia, Senegal gum and Indian gum

e415.desc: XANTHAN GUM is a polysaccharide with many industrial uses, including as a common food additive.

e418.desc: A polysaccharide produced through fermentation of the bacterium Sphingomonas elodea, originally isolated from a pond in the United States and now manufactured globally, with major production in Asia and the Americas. It's made by fermenting sugar with the bacteria, then purifying and drying the resulting gum into a fine powder. Gellan gum is virtually tasteless and odorless, making it ideal as a texturizing agent. Widely used in dairy products, plant-based beverages, desserts, jams, and bakery items to provide gelling, thickening, and stabilizing properties. Nutritionally, it's a non-digestible fiber, contributing negligible calories and no significant vitamins or minerals to the diet.

n.en: Glycerol ester of tall oil rosin

e450i.desc: SODIUM ACID PYROPHOSPHATE is an additive used to prevent the formation of crystals and discoloration of the crab meat.

e450iii.desc: TETRASODIUM PYROPHOSPHATE, also called sodium pyrophosphate, tetrasodium phosphate or TSPP, is a colorless transparent crystalline chemical compound with the formula Na4P2O7.

e460.desc: CELLULOSE is an organic compound with the formula -C6H10O5-n, a polysaccharide consisting of a linear chain of several hundred to many thousands of linked D-glucose units. Cellulose is used as emulsifier, thickener and stabilizer in processed foods. Cellulose powder is, for example, used in processed cheese to prevent caking inside the package.

e461.desc: METHYL CELLULOSE is a chemical compound derived from cellulose. Methyl cellulose is added to food products, to generate their characteristic thick consistency, for example ice cream or croquette.

e500.desc: SODIUM CARBONATES is the generic term for a Na and CO3 combination.

e500i.desc: SODIUM CARBONATE, -also known as washing soda, soda ash and soda crystals, and in the monohydrate form as crystal carbonate- is the water-soluble sodium salt of carbonic acid.

e500ii.desc: SODIUM BICARBONATE -sodium hydrogen carbonate-, commonly known as baking soda, is a chemical compound with the formula NaHCO3.

e503.desc: Also known as "hartshorn" or baker's ammonia, this mineral salt was historically produced by heating animal horn, and is now made synthetically by reacting ammonia with carbon dioxide. It has a sharp, ammonia-like smell and salty, alkaline taste that fully dissipates during baking. Traditionally used in home baking for thin, crisp goods like gingerbread and speculaas, it remains far more prevalent industrially, valued for its low cost, stability, and moisture-free leavening—ideal for high-speed cracker and cookie production. Nutritionally inert, it serves purely as a leavening agent, contributing no calories or nutrients to the final product.

e503i.desc: AMMONIUM CARBONATE is a salt with the chemical formula -NH4-2CO3. Since it readily degrades to gaseous ammonia and carbon dioxide upon heating, it is used as a leavening agent. It is also known as baker's ammonia and was a predecessor to the more modern leavening agents baking soda and baking powder.

e503ii.desc: AMMONIUM BICARBONATE is an inorganic compound with formula -NH4-HCO3, simplified to NH5CO3. Ammonium bicarbonate is used in the food industry as a raising agent for flat baked goods, such as cookies and crackers, and in China in steamed buns and Chinese almond cookies. It was commonly used in the home before modern day baking powder was made available.

e504i.desc: MAGNESIUM CARBONATE, MgCO3 -archaic name magnesia alba-, is an inorganic salt that is a white solid.

e510.desc: AMMONIUM CHLORIDE is an inorganic compound with the formula NH4Cl and a white crystalline salt that is highly soluble in water.

e579.desc: IRONII GLUCONATE, or ferrous gluconate,[1] is a black compound often used as an iron supplement. It is the iron-II- salt of gluconic acid.

e621.desc: MONOSODIUM GLUTAMATE -MSG, also known as sodium glutamate- is the sodium salt of glutamic acid, one of the most abundant naturally occurring non-essential amino acids.

e953.desc: ISOMALT is a sugar substitute, a type of sugar alcohol used primarily for its sugar-like physical properties. It has little to no impact on blood sugar levels, and does not stimulate the release of insulin. Isomalt is widely used for the production of sugar-free candy, especially hard-boiled candy.

e954.desc: Sodium saccharin -benzoic sulfimide- is an artificial sweetener with effectively no food energy.

n.en: Rebaudioside from multiple gene donors expressed in Yarrowia lipolityca

e965.desc: MALTITOL is a sugar alcohol -a polyol- used as a sugar substitute. It has 75–90% of the sweetness of sucrose -table sugar- and nearly identical properties, except for browning. Maltitol's high sweetness allows it to be used without being mixed with other sweeteners. It is used in candy manufacture, particularly sugar-free hard candy, chewing gum, chocolates, baked goods, and ice cream.

n.en: alpha-Amylase from Bacillus megaterium expressed in Bacillus subtilis

e1104.desc: A LIPASE is any enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of fats -lipids-. Lipases serve important roles in human practices as ancient as yogurt and cheese fermentation. Lipases are generally animal sourced, but can also be sourced microbially.
